title: Redwood Operational Compact: Policies, Workflows, and Templates
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Summary
This document is Redwood Inference’s Operational Compact: a concise, company-wide reference that collects the core policies, approval workflows, and templates teams must use for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, travel, and internal templates. It is designed for product, engineering, and business teams to reduce ambiguity and speed routine decisions while preserving compliance and auditability.

Scope and intent
- Scope: applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and contingent workers.
- Intent: create a single, maintained source of truth for recurring operational decisions and approvals.
- Exceptions: documented exceptions require a risk ticket and signoff by the owning domain and security/legal where applicable. See "Risk and Exceptions" related page.

1) Access & Permissions (RBAC and request patterns)
Purpose: minimize blast radius while enabling engineering velocity.
Core principles:
- Least privilege by default: new accounts receive role-based baseline privileges, not owner-level access.
- Temporary elevation: use time-bound privilege grants for debugging or incident response with mandatory justification.
- Separation of duties: provisioning, approval, and audit must be distinct actors where practical.

Role catalog (examples)
- system-viewer: read-only dashboards, logs, billing metadata.
- developer: deploy to non-prod, create feature branches, access dev-only datasets.
- service-operator: manage runtime configs, restart services, run approved runbooks.
- infra-admin: create cloud infra (limited to infra team).
- security-auditor: read-only access to audit logs and alert feeds.

Access request workflow (standard requests)
1. Requestor opens an Access Request (template: access-request-template.csv) in the Access Portal.
2. Owner (service/team) reviews justification and assigns role.
3. Manager approves (or auto-approves for entry-level roles).
4. System grants access with a 30-day default expiry.
5. Access is reviewed at 30 days; if still required, an extension is sought via the portal.

Emergency elevation (incident-only)
1. Oncall provides short justification in the incident ticket and tags the change as "urgent-access".
2. Pager duty lead or SRE manager approves within 90 minutes.
3. Elevation expires automatically at timestamp + 6 hours unless extended by SRE director.
4. Post-incident, the requester must document cause and approvals in the incident review within 5 business days.

Audit and periodic review
- Quarterly role entitlement reviews are run by people-ops and team owners. Findings are tracked and closed within 30 days.
- Audit logs retained per data classification policy (section 3).

2) Change Management (routine, minor, major)
Purpose: ensure risk is understood and mitigations are in place before changes reach production.
Change categories and approval matrix
- Routine (low risk): configuration tweaks, UI copy updates. Approval: service owner. CAB notification optional. Typical lead time: same day.
- Minor (medium risk): deployment of non-breaking infra changes, database index additions. Approval: service owner + SRE reviewer. CAB notification required. Typical lead time: 48–72 hours.
- Major (high risk): schema migrations impacting production, global config flips, model rollouts with >1% expected customer impact. Approval: service owner + SRE lead + product lead + security review + CAB signoff. Typical lead time: 5 business days.

Change request procedure (engineers)
1. Open a Change Request (CR) in the Change Portal. Include: description, risk assessment, rollback plan, test plan, outage window.
2. Automated checks run: unit/test coverage, canary config, dependency list.
3. Reviewer(s) provide comments; for Major changes schedule an RFC review with stakeholders.
4. Schedule a deployment window. For Major changes, document an explicit rollback plan and a smoke test checklist.
5. Execute change; monitor key SLOs for 60 minutes post-deploy. Fail fast and rollback if SLO degradation > 5% or error budget consumed.

Emergency change path
- Emergency changes must be declared in the incident channel and include a post-facto CR within 24 hours. Emergency approvals follow the incident escalation path.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Scheduled maintenance windows: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for platform-level maintenance with 72-hour notice.
- Blackout: no non-critical Major changes during high-traffic global launches or contracted customer SLA windows (product PM to declare).

3) Data Management (classification, retention, access, and transfer)
Purpose: protect user/customer data and meet regulatory and contractual obligations.
Data classification levels
- Public: safe to publish externally.
- Internal: operational metadata and engineering logs without PII. Retention: 1 year unless needed for analytics.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, model artifacts containing customer inputs. Retention: contractual baseline or 7 years where required.
- Restricted: regulated data, legal hold, or HSM-protected keys. Access: strictly limited; requires security + legal approval.

Retention and deletion rules
- Backups: encrypted; retention default 90 days for non-confidential, configurable for longer on request.
- Logs: system and audit logs retained 1 year; security logs retained 3 years.
- Embeddings & model inputs: default policy is to not persist customer inputs in hosted environments unless contractually agreed; if persisted classify as Confidential and tag accordingly.

Data transfer and egress controls
- All cross-region transfers must use approved encryption-in-transit and be recorded.
- Sensitive exports require an export ticket and must be scanned for PII by the Data Steward.

Data access request (for analytics or research)
1. Submit Data Request Form with purpose, dataset, retention, and access duration.
2. Data Steward reviews for purpose legitimacy and PII exposure.
3. Approval chain: dataset owner -> security -> legal (if customer data involved).
4. Approved datasets provisioned into project-scoped, time-limited views.

4) Procurement & Expenses (thresholds, approvals, and templates)
Purpose: standardize buying behavior while enabling teams to move quickly.
Approval thresholds (net of taxes)
- < $2,500: team lead approval; P-card preferred.
- $2,500–$25,000: department manager + finance review.
- $25,001–$150,000: procurement + finance + legal review.
- > $150,000: executive sponsor + procurement committee + legal + finance.

Purchase types and timelines
- Cloud/usage commitments: present a forecast and unit economics analysis to finance; minimum 10 business days lead time.
- Software subscriptions: procurement leads contract negotiation with standard SDLAs; do not sign vendor EULAs without legal present for >$25k annual spend.

Expense reimbursement policy
- Submit receipts within 14 days via Expenses Portal. Lost receipts require manager approval and reasonable attestation.
- Per diem: domestic $75/day; international region banded per policy table (see attached template).

Procurement checklist (required attachments)
- Business justification (one paragraph).
- Vendor W-9 or equivalent tax document.
- Security questionnaire for SaaS vendors (if storing customer data).
- Signed SOW or contract draft for > $25k.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
Purpose: reduce third-party risk and ensure service continuity.
Pre-onboarding steps
1. Vendor intake form: scope, data access requirements, financial terms.
2. Security assessment threshold: if vendor will process Confidential or Restricted data, route to Security Review.
3. Procurement validates pricing and commercial terms.

Onboarding checklist
- Contract executed (legal).
- Security controls verified (access scope, MFA, segmented network access).
- Escalation contacts added to vendor directory and PagerDuty if SLA requires.
- Backup and exit-plan defined (data retrieval and deletion semantics).

Vendor performance SLAs & review cadence
- Standard operational SLA: 99.9% monthly availability unless contractually agreed otherwise.
- Quarterly vendor health review for strategic vendors, annual review for non-strategic.

Termination and offboarding
- Trigger exit checklist: revoke accounts, collect final invoices, verify data return/deletion per contract.
- Retain termination artifacts for 7 years if vendor managed Confidential or Restricted data.

6) Travel Policy (business travel approvals, expenses, safety)
Purpose: allow safe, compliant travel while controlling costs.
Pre-travel approvals
- Domestic: manager pre-approval; travel booked through approved vendor portal.
- International: manager + people-ops approval; ensure passport and visa validity and check travel advisories.

Booking and permitted classes
- Flights: economy for trips < 6 hours; premium economy permissible for trips > 6 hours with manager approval.
- Hotels: standard business hotels; use negotiated corporate rate when available.
- Ground transport: rideshare or car rental (if required for remote client locations).

Expense submission and deadlines
- Submit all travel receipts and travel report within 14 days of trip end.
- Include: itinerary, meeting notes, client contact; missing items require manager attestation.

Safety and emergency
- People-ops maintains an emergency contact list. In case of safety incidents during travel, provide immediate notice to Security and people-ops.

7) Internal Templates and Examples (where to find and conventions)
- Access Request Template: access-request-template.csv (fields: requestor, team, role, justification, duration, owner).
- Change Request Template: change-request-template.md (fields: summary, risk, rollback, smoke-tests, runbook ref).
- Procurement Brief: procurement-brief-template.docx (fields: business-case, forecast, vendor-comparison).
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: vendor-security-scan.xlsx.
- Expense Template: travel-expense-template.xlsx.

Naming and documentation conventions
- File names: kebab-case and include year when relevant (e.g., project-name-2025-retrospective.md).
- Ownership: every document requires an owner tag and a review cadence in the metadata header.

Governance, exceptions, and periodic review
- Policy steward: people-ops owns this compact and coordinates cross-functional reviews.
- Review cadence: full compact reviewed annually; topical updates (e.g., procurement thresholds) may be updated as needed with a notice period.
- Exceptions: any deviation must be recorded in the Risk & Exceptions page with approval chain.

Appendices
A. Quick approval contact list
- People-ops (policy steward): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Procurement lead: procurement@redwood.ai
- Security intake: security-intake@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-ops@redwood.ai

B. Example: Minor Change smoke test checklist
- Verify health checks pass for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Confirm error rate unchanged within ±1% of baseline.
- Validate representative customer request end-to-end.

C. Example: Vendor onboarding summary (required fields)
- Vendor name
- Primary contact and escalation contact
- Data types processed and storage locations
- Contract start/end and renewal terms
- Onboarding owner and date

How to request updates to this compact
- File an update request via Confluence inline comments or email people-ops@redwood.ai with suggested wording, rationale, and reviewer names. People-ops will triage and publish changes following the review cadence.

Policy change history
- 2024-02-12: initial compact published (Maya Thompson).
- 2024-10-03: added emergency elevation workflow (SRE feedback).
- 2025-03-18: updated procurement thresholds and travel per diem bands.
- 2025-08-01: expanded data retention table and vendor SLA guidance.

End of document
